# Olipop prepares for growth with new CEO

olipop.jpg

Ben Goodwin, left, is transitioning from founder and chief executive officer of Olipop to chairman and head of innovation. Christian Patiño Webb has been named the company’s new CEO.

 | Photo: Olipop

08.12.2026

By Brooke Just

GoogleAdd as a preferred  
source on Google

OAKLAND, CALIF. — Functional soda company Olipop has named Christian Patiño Webb as its new chief executive officer to support its next stage of growth.

Patiño Webb succeeds Ben Goodwin, founder and CEO, who is transitioning to executive chairman and head of innovation for the company. [...] Goodwin, who founded the company in 2018 to support digestive health, will focus on the company’s long-term vision, advance innovation and also shape its next phase of growth while also stewarding its mission, values and culture and will work in partnership with Patiño Webb.

Patiño Webb comes to Olipop from Electrolit, where he most recently was CEO.

During his career, Patiño Webb also has worked for Procter & Gamble, Johnson & Johnson, Red Bull and Unilever. [...] “Founding and leading Olipop to mainstream success has been the honor of my lifetime, and I feel extremely fortunate and proud of what we’ve accomplished to date," Goodwin said. “The team and I spent significant time carefully selecting a CEO and Christian unequivocally rose to the top. His clear track record of scaling consumer brands that have a focus on product quality and are driven by a strong founder vision make him a fantastic fit for the next leg of our journey. In addition to that, his character is exactly what we look for in an Olipop leader—strong principles and humility combined with a robust competitive hunger.”

Olipop has been scaling its functional soda – formulated with a blend of plant fiber, prebiotics and botanicals – in recent years.

Olipop (stylized as OLIPOP) is a prebiotic "Prebiotic (nutrition)") soft drink produced in the United States. It is sold in over 65,000 retailers nationwide and the company is valued $1.85 billion as of February 2025. The drink's marketing claims that it improves gut health.

The brand name Olipop is a portmanteau of the prebiotic "Prebiotic (nutrition)") fiber oligosaccharide (oli), and "pop", a common name for a soft drink in the United States.

His take on why it worked is simple. People respond to real innovation. Conglomerates push products out and call it a day. When you put money down you want something genuine in return.   
  
Watch the full CEO Series episode with Ben Goodwin on the Executive House YouTube channel. Link in bio.
